api.review:
Independent source review at 440e738110c632cc62d8096624b086b7c30f0bfc, against base 97a48303a654ae1d2bf3c0e167f5a94590cea8aa: no identified blocking findings.

I reviewed all 14 changed paths and traced the production changes through the SQL scanner and claim paths, delivery retry scheduling, inbox outcome propagation, persisted lesson state, prompt lookup and catalogue filtering. The scanner and claimant use the same predecessor-waiting predicate; an exhausted pending or failed predecessor releases its follower, while a sending predecessor with a live lease still blocks. Retryable outcomes schedule a delayed queue wake after the store records the retry; a lost wake retains the scanner backstop. Caught handler failures no longer log as handled. Newly persisted turns require the delivered force-reply text to match the saved prompt in the same chat. Historical turns without promptText retain the documented force-reply fallback. The catalogue length bound and chat backstop avoid grading an unseen truncated line.

The GitHub read at 2026-10-13 14:00 UTC shows all 13 hosted checks successful on this exact head, including the required PostgreSQL aggregate and its five general shards, namespace, recovery, PostgreSQL 18 shape, check and secret-boundary. Source: https://github.com/pirate-social-club/api-next/actions/runs/38402056308 . I inspected the added assertions and hosted check bindings; I did not rerun the native API suites in this reviewer session.

One nonblocking documentation correction: the retry comment says Queues accepts at most 12 hours. The current primary documentation permits integer delaySeconds from 0 through 86400 (24 hours): https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/configuration/javascript-apis/ . The chosen 43200 cap is valid and longer waits retain the scanner fallback; describe it as the selected cap rather than the platform maximum.

The cloud coordinator remains the product writer and may integrate this reviewed head through the authorized squash-merge path after its fresh head/check/custody checks. This review clears the six delivery source findings. Staging migration and effective-role readiness, serving bindings and the new phone acceptance remain separate technical requirements.

solid.head: e86f34d118b56d7e0d9405c5bdea7ba41ee989eb
solid.review:
Independent source review at e86f34d118b56d7e0d9405c5bdea7ba41ee989eb, against base 5dae654a688c81851961bfaa84bb17648a9460ed: hold integration for one blocking finding.

The probe gate and privacy classifier compare exact, case-sensitive path strings, but the pinned @solidjs/router 2.0.0-next.16 matcher accepts one trailing slash and compares static segments case-insensitively. For example, /internal/telegram-login-probe/, /INTERNAL/TELEGRAM-LOGIN-PROBE and /internal/telegram-login-probe/callback/ match the probe routes while both isTelegramProbePage and isTelegramLinkPage return false.

This skips the SSR refusal in src/entry-server.tsx:55-60 for production, unconfigured, expired and non-hydrating/alternate-asset contexts. It also skips request/query scrubbing at entry-server.tsx:62-66 and the private/no-store, no-referrer and noindex middleware response policy. Callback code and state remain available to the request event and router during SSR. Browser origin and expiry checks still refuse provider actions, but they do not restore the missing server gate or prevent SSR from seeing those callback values.

I reproduced this using the actual installed matcher at version 2.0.0-next.16 and TypeScript-transpiled, in-memory copies of the exact fetched PR modules: config blob a4fd9330008d9f23d35d891e920a2d5ab00ee564 and privacy blob c8cc8925fe353bb96accce9e541d6a57cdf8090d. Of eight URLs (the two canonical routes, each with a trailing slash, uppercase segments and uppercase plus slash), all eight match their routes. Only the two canonical URLs trigger the gate and scrub; the other six retain fixture callback values in the effective SSR request. This is a router/classifier/control-flow reproduction, not a deployed Worker or full SSR-render observation.

Please make the gate and privacy classifier cover every route spelling the router admits, or reject/canonicalize those aliases before routing and privacy-sensitive rendering. Add actual entry-server plus middleware regression cases for mixed-case and trailing-slash entry and callback URLs: production, missing canonical origin, expiry, disabled hydration and alternate asset origin must refuse; allowed staging callbacks must remove fixture code/state from the request event, router search and HTML, including error responses, and retain the private response headers. Carry equivalent coverage for the existing Telegram linking routes if their shared classifier changes.

All three applicable hosted checks passed on this exact head; Solid Doctor (main) was skipped. Those checks currently cover only canonical probe paths, so they do not clear this finding. Source: https://github.com/pirate-social-club/pirate-web-solid/actions/runs/38402093458 .

The cloud coordinator keeps exclusive source custody. Please fix this on the designated branch, publish the corrected head, rerun hosted checks and return it for independent re-review. The fixed expiry remains 2026-10-17T00:00:00Z; the pending owner decision and follow-up Recovery/Connect design remain outside this probe source acceptance.

result.verification: Actual router matcher and exact fetched PR classifier modules; server guard and scrub condition evaluated without starting a Worker or SSR renderer.
